correctness.rationale: For each oriented pair of the order 2h+1 tournament the clockwise pair-gap sizes are a=d-1 and b=h-d, summing to h-1. Inductively defined threshold formulas of rank r use only three variables and detect every a,b threshold through 2^r-1; combining them inside two outer quantifiers distinguishes every smaller half-order h<2^(q-1)-1. The other direction uses a doubled 2n-circle with actual even vertices and ghost odd antipodes. Corresponding marker gaps stay either exactly equal or parity-matched and both at least L_r=2^(r+1)-1; the parity-constrained splitting lemma with L_r=2L_(r-1)+1 proves a q-round unrestricted EF winning strategy when both orders are at least 2^q-1. Independently executed program verified 18,600 threshold-formula instances and exact FO^3 rank types for odd orders 3..39 through rank 5. The finite run was not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a canonical family of regular locally transitive tournaments, the theorem gives a natural complete rank-by-rank model-theoretic classification, exact sharp stabilization at order 2^q-1, precise number of equivalence classes, and minimum rank distinguishing two sizes. The fact that three variables suffice for all distinctions visible to unrestricted q-round logic is a substantive expressiveness theorem, not a single bounded computation or a shallow parameter substitution. The uniform construction of threshold formulas and matching full EF upper proof makes the exact bound reusable in related interpretations.
